correctness.rationale: On the sum-zero torus E, the derivative I+hK diag(cos z) is singular first when Rayleigh equality selects the top cycle eigenspace and the corresponding highest-frequency eigenvector vanishes wherever cos z>-1. For even n the top eigenvector is alternating and nonzero everywhere, giving only all pi; for odd n any top eigenvector has at most one zero, so closure forces exactly one zero phase among pi entries and n cyclic positions. Both have one-dimensional nullity. The analytic odd Lyapunov–Schmidt reduction gives cubic coefficient sum_i w_i^4/6=1/(6n) even or 1/(4n) odd and three near-critical preimages at amplitudes ±sqrt(6n mu), ±sqrt(4n mu) plus O_n(mu^(3/2)). Uniform all n>=3 follows analytically. Independent eigenvector checks n=3..16 had <1e-10 residual, not proof of all n.
